cohort: Pregnant women (N=1074 at baseline, N=753 at follow-up)
finding: Pregnant women with high sense of coherence were less likely to experience caesarean section and more likely to experience assisted vaginal birth.
mod_finding: Higher sense of coherence was associated with lower likelihood of caesarean section and higher likelihood of assisted vaginal birth.  Women's sense of coherence increased with birth satisfaction and decreased with epidural, assisted vaginal birth, and decreased birth satisfaction.
